```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"math/rand"
	"runtime"
	"sort"
	"time"
)

// Message represents a message with an ID and payload
type Message struct {
	ID      int
	Payload string
}

// Router handles routing messages to consumers
type Router struct {
	inputChan   chan Message
	outputChans []chan Message
	workers     int
	latencyChan chan time.Duration
}

// NewRouter initializes a new router with specified number of workers and consumers
func NewRouter(workers, consumers int) *Router {
	inputChan := make(chan Message, 10000) // Buffered channel for high throughput
	outputChans := make([]chan Message, consumers)
	for i := 0; i < consumers; i++ {
		outputChans[i] = make(chan Message, 1000)
	}
	latencyChan := make(chan time.Duration, 1000)
	return &Router{
		inputChan:   inputChan,
		outputChans: outputChans,
		workers:     workers,
		latencyChan: latencyChan,
	}
}

// Start starts the router's worker goroutines
func (r *Router) Start() {
	for i := 0; i < r.workers; i++ {
		go func(workerID int) {
			for msg := range r.inputChan {
				start := time.Now()
				// Simulate routing logic (e.g., round-robin to consumers)
				consumerID := workerID % len(r.outputChans)
				r.outputChans[consumerID] <- msg
				latency := time.Since(start)
				r.latencyChan <- latency
			}
		}(i)
	}
}

// MonitorLatency periodically prints the average latency
func (r *Router) MonitorLatency() {
	ticker := time.NewTicker(1 * time.Second)
	defer ticker.Stop()

	var latencies []time.Duration

	for range ticker.C {
		if len(latencies) > 0 {
			sort.Slice(latencies, func(i, j int) bool {
				return latencies[i] < latencies[j]
			})
			avg := time.Duration(0)
			for _, l := range latencies {
				avg += l
			}
			avg /= time.Duration(len(latencies))
			fmt.Printf("Latency stats (last %d messages):\n", len(latencies))
			fmt.Printf("  Min: %v\n", latencies[0])
			fmt.Printf("  Max: %v\n", latencies[len(latencies)-1])
			fmt.Printf("  Avg: %v\n", avg)
			latencies = nil
		}
	}
}

// Producer generates messages and sends them to the router
func (r *Router) Produce(numMessages int) {
	for i := 0; i < numMessages; i++ {
		r.inputChan <- Message{
			ID:      i,
			Payload: fmt.Sprintf("Message-%d", i),
		}
	}
	close(r.inputChan)
}

// Consumer reads messages from output channels and simulates processing
func (r *Router) Consume() {
	for _, ch := range r.outputChans {
		go func(ch chan Message) {
			for msg := range ch {
				// Simulate message processing
				time.Sleep(time.Duration(rand.Intn(10)) * time.Microsecond)
				fmt.Printf("Consumer processed message: %d\n", msg.ID)
			}
		}(ch)
	}
}

func main() {
	runtime.GOMAXPROCS(runtime.NumCPU())

	// Initialize the router with 10 workers and 5 consumers
	router := NewRouter(10, 5)

	// Start monitoring latency
	go router.MonitorLatency()

	// Start consumers
	router.Consume()

	// Start the router
	router.Start()

	// Produce 1 million messages
	go router.Produce(1_000_000)

	// Keep the main goroutine alive
	select {}
}
```

```cpp
struct Message {

class MessageQueue {
public:
    void enqueue(const Message& msg) {
        std::unique_lock<std::mutex> lock(mtx);
        queue.push(msg);
        cond.notify_one();
    }

    Message dequeue() {
        std::unique_lock<std::mutex> lock(mtx);
        cond.wait(lock, [this]{ return !queue.empty(); });
        Message msg = queue.front();
        queue.pop();
        return msg;
    }

private:
    std::queue<Message> queue;
    std::mutex mtx;
    std::condition_variable cond;
};

class LatencyMonitor {
public:
    void recordLatency(std::chrono::microseconds latency) {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mtx);
        total += latency;
        count++;
        if (latency < min) min = latency;
        if (latency > max) max = latency;
    }

    void printStats() {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mtx);
        if (count == 0) return;
        std::cout << "Average latency: " << total / count.count() << " microseconds\n";
        std::cout << "Min latency: " << min.count() << " microseconds\n";
        std::cout << "Max latency: " << max.count() << " microseconds\n";
    }

private:
    std::mutex mtx;
    std::chrono::microseconds total = 0;
    int count = 0;
    std::chrono::microseconds min = std::chrono::microseconds::max();

        queue.enqueue(shutdownMsg);
    }

        monitor.recordLatency(latency);
```

```cpp
// Thread-safe message queue
class MessageQueue {
public:
    void push(const Message& msg) {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mtx_);
        queue_.push(msg);
        cv_.notify_one();
    }

    Message pop() {
        std::unique_lock<std::mutex> lock(mtx_);
        cv_.wait(lock, [this]{ return !queue_.empty(); });
        Message msg = queue_.front();
        queue_.pop();
        return msg;
    }

private:
    std::queue<Message> queue_;
    std::mutex mtx_;
    std::condition_variable cv_;
};

// Latency monitor with average and max tracking
class LatencyMonitor {
public:
    void record(double latency) {

        total_ += latency;
        count_++;
        if (latency > max_) {
            max_ = latency;
        }
    }

    void report() {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mtx_);
        if (count_ == 0) return;
        double avg = total_ / count_;
        std::cout << "Average latency: " << avg << " us, Max latency: " << max_ << " us\n";
        total_ = 0.0;
        count_ = 0;
        max_ = 0.0;
    }

private:

    double max_ = 0.0;

};
```

```c
void packet_handler(u_char *user, const struct pcap_pkthdr *pkthdr, const u_char *packet);

int main(int argc, char *argv[]) {
    char errbuf[PCAP_ERRBUF_SIZE];
    pcap_t *handle;
    char *dev = pcap_lookupdev(errbuf);
    if (dev == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Error finding device: %s\n", errbuf);
        return 1;
    }

    // Open the device for capturing
    handle = pcap_open_live(dev, BUFSIZ, 1, 1000, errbuf);
    if (handle == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Error opening device: %s\n", errbuf);
        return 1;
    }

    // Set a filter: only capture IP packets
    struct bpf_program fp;
    char filter_exp[] = "ip";
    if (pcap_compile(handle, &fp, filter_exp, 0, PCAP_NETMASK_UNKNOWN) == -1) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Error compiling filter: %s\n", pcap_geterr(handle));
        return 1;
    }
    if (pcap_setfilter(handle, &fp) == -1) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Error setting filter: %s\n", pcap_geterr(handle));
        return 1;
    }

    // Start capturing packets
    pcap_loop(handle, 0, packet_handler, NULL);

    pcap_close(handle);
    return 0;
}

void packet_handler(u_char *user, const struct pcap_pkthdr *pkthdr, const u_char *packet) {
    // Ethernet header is always first
    const struct ether_header *eth_hdr = (struct ether_header *)packet;
    if (ntohs(eth_hdr->ether_type) != ETHERTYPE_IP) {
        return; // Not an IP packet
    }

    // IP header
    const struct ip *ip_hdr = (struct ip *)(packet + sizeof(struct ether_header));
    if (ip_hdr->ip_p != IPPROTO_TCP && ip_hdr->ip_p != IPPROTO_UDP) {
        return; // Only forward TCP/UDP
    }

    // Forward the packet (example: send to another IP address)
    int sockfd = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_RAW, IPPROTO_RAW);
    if (sockfd < 0) {
        perror("Socket creation failed");
        return;
    }

    struct sockaddr_in dest_addr;
    dest_addr.sin_family = AF_INET;
    inet_pton(AF_INET, "192.168.1.100", &dest_addr.sin_addr); // Forward to this IP

    // Send the packet (we skip IP checksum for simplicity)
    sendto(sockfd, packet, pkthdr->caplen, 0, (struct sockaddr *)&dest_addr, sizeof(dest_addr));
    close(sockfd);
}
```

```c
void set_promiscuous_mode(int sockfd, const char *iface) {
    struct ifreq ifr;
    strcpy(ifr.ifr_name, iface);
    if (ioctl(sockfd, SIOCGIFFLAGS, &ifr) == -1) {
        perror("ioctl SIOCGIFFLAGS");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);

    ifr.ifr_flags |= IFF_PROMISC;
    if (ioctl(sockfd, SIOCSIFFLAGS, &ifr) == -1) {

        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }

void forward_packet(const char *iface, const unsigned char *packet, int len) {
    int sockfd = socket(AF_PACKET, SOCK_RAW, htons(ETH_P_ALL));
    if (sockfd == -1) {
        perror("socket");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }

    struct ifreq ifr;
    strcpy(ifr.ifr_name, iface);
    if (ioctl(sockfd, SIOCGIFINDEX, &ifr) == -1) {
        perror("ioctl SIOCGIFINDEX");
        close(sockfd);
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);

    struct sockaddr_ll sll;
    memset(&sll, 0, sizeof(sll));
    sll.sll_ifindex = ifr.ifr_ifindex;
```

---

### ✅ **Key Features Implemented**
- **Packet Capture**: Uses `libpcap` for low-latency packet capture.
- **Packet Filtering**: Filters packets based on source IP and destination port.
- **Packet Forwarding**: Uses raw sockets to forward packets to a target interface.

### 📦 **Code: Ultra-Low-Latency Networking Service**

```c
#include <pcap.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <netinet/ip.h>
#include <netinet/tcp.h>
#include <arpa/inet.h>
#include <sys/socket.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#define FILTER_SOURCE_IP "192.168.1.100"
#define FILTER_DEST_PORT 80
#define FORWARD_INTERFACE "eth0"
#define FORWARD_IP "192.168.1.200"

// Function to parse and forward the packet
void packet_handler(u_char *user, const struct pcap_pkthdr *pkthdr, const u_char *packet) {
    struct ip *ip_header = (struct ip *)(packet + 14); // Ethernet header is 14 bytes
    struct tcphdr *tcp_header = (struct tcphdr *)(packet + 14 + sizeof(struct ip));
    struct sockaddr_in forward_addr;

    // Filter based on source IP and destination port
    if (ntohl(ip_header->ip_src.s_addr) == inet_addr(FILTER_SOURCE_IP) &&
        ntohs(tcp_header->th_dport) == FILTER_DEST_PORT) {

        // Forward the packet to the target interface
        int sockfd = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_RAW, IPPROTO_RAW);
        if (sockfd < 0) {
            perror("socket");
            return;
        }

        forward_addr.sin_family = AF_INET;
        forward_addr.sin_addr.s_addr = inet_addr(FORWARD_IP);
        forward_addr.sin_port = 0;

        if (sendto(sockfd, packet, pkthdr->len, 0, (struct sockaddr *)&forward_addr, sizeof(forward_addr)) < 0) {
            perror("sendto");
        }

        close(sockfd);
    }
}

int main() {
    char errbuf[PCAP_ERRBUF_SIZE];
    pcap_t *handle = pcap_open_live("eth0", BUFSIZ, 1, 1000, errbuf);

    if (!handle) {
        fprintf(stderr, "pcap_open_live: %s\n", errbuf);
        return 1;
    }

    // Set filter: source IP and destination port
    struct bpf_program fp;
    char filter_exp[] = "ip src 192.168.1.100 and tcp dst port 80";
    if (pcap_compile(handle, &fp, filter_exp, 0, PCAP_NETMASK_UNKNOWN) == -1) {
        fprintf(stderr, "pcap_compile: %s\n", pcap_geterr(handle));
        return 1;
    }

    if (pcap_setfilter(handle, &fp) == -1) {
        fprintf(stderr, "pcap_setfilter: %s\n", pcap_geterr(handle));
        return 1;
    }

    // Start packet capture
    pcap_loop(handle, 0, packet_handler, NULL);

    pcap_close(handle);
    return 0;
}
```

```c
#define BACKUP_SUFFIX ".bak"
#define MAX_BACKUPS 5
#define SLEEP_INTERVAL 60  // seconds

void daemonize() {
    pid_t pid = fork();
    if (pid < 0) {
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }
    if (pid > 0) {
        exit(EXIT_SUCCESS);
    }

    if (setsid() < 0) {
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }

    umask(0);
    chdir("/");
    close(STDIN_FILENO);
    close(STDOUT_FILENO);
    close(STDERR_FILENO);
}

void rotate_log(const char *log_file) {
    struct stat st;
    if (stat(log_file, &st) < 0) {
        return;  // File does not exist
    }

    if (st.st_size >= MAX_LOG_SIZE) {
        char backup[256];
        snprintf(backup, sizeof(backup), "%s%s", log_file, BACKUP_SUFFIX);

        // Rename log to backup
        if (rename(log_file, backup) < 0) {
            return;
        }

        // Truncate the original log file
        int fd = open(log_file, O_WRONLY | O_TRUNC | O_CREAT, 0644);
        if (fd >= 0) {
            close(fd);
        }

        // Compress the backup using gzip
        char cmd[256];
        snprintf(cmd, sizeof(cmd), "gzip %s", backup);
        system(cmd);
    }

void sig_handler(int signum) {
    if (signum == SIGTERM || signum == SIGINT) {
        exit(EXIT_SUCCESS);
    }

    signal(SIGINT, sig_handler);

    daemonize();

    while (1) {
        rotate_log(LOG_FILE);
        sleep(SLEEP_INTERVAL);
    }

    return 0;
}
```

```c
        perror("open source");
        return;

        close(src_fd);
        return;

    ssize_t bytes_read;

    while ((bytes_read = read(src_fd, buffer, BUFFER_SIZE)) > 0) {
        write(dst_fd, buffer, bytes_read);
    }

    close(src_fd);
    close(dst_fd);

    if (truncate(LOG_FILE, 0) == -1) {
        perror("truncate");
    }

}
```

Here's a minimal, memory-efficient log rotation daemon written in C for a constrained environment. It rotates logs when they exceed a size limit, keeps a limited number of backups, and avoids memory-intensive operations like loading entire files into memory.

```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <sys/types.h>
#include <sys/stat.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <signal.h>
#include <time.h>
#include <dirent.h>
#include <syslog.h>

#define LOG_FILE "/var/log/app.log"
#define MAX_LOG_SIZE (1024 * 1024 * 10)  // 10MB
#define MAX_BACKUPS 5
#define BACKUP_DIR "/var/log/backups"
#define GZIP_CMD "gzip"

// Daemonize the process
void daemonize() {
    pid_t pid = fork();
    if (pid < 0) {
        syslog(LOG_ERR, "Fork failed");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }
    if (pid > 0) {
        exit(EXIT_SUCCESS);
    }

    if (setsid() < 0) {
        syslog(LOG_ERR, "setsid failed");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }

    umask(0);
    chdir("/");
    close(STDIN_FILENO);
    close(STDOUT_FILENO);
    close(STDERR_FILENO);
}

// Rotate the log file
void rotate_log() {
    char log_file[256];
    char backup_file[256];
    char gzip_cmd[256];
    struct stat st;

    snprintf(log_file, sizeof(log_file), "%s", LOG_FILE);

    // Check if log file exists and is large enough
    if (stat(log_file, &st) < 0) {
        syslog(LOG_ERR, "Log file does not exist: %s", log_file);
        return;
    }

    if (st.st_size < MAX_LOG_SIZE) {
        return;
    }

    // Create backup filename with timestamp
    time_t now = time(NULL);
    struct tm *tm = localtime(&now);
    snprintf(backup_file, sizeof(backup_file), "%s.%04d%02d%02d%02d%02d%02d",
             LOG_FILE, tm->tm_year + 1900, tm->tm_mon + 1, tm->tm_mday,
             tm->tm_hour, tm->tm_min, tm->tm_sec);

    // Rename original log to backup
    if (rename(log_file, backup_file) < 0) {
        syslog(LOG_ERR, "Failed to rename log file: %s", log_file);
        return;
    }

    // Compress the backup
    snprintf(gzip_cmd, sizeof(gzip_cmd), "%s %s", GZIP_CMD, backup_file);
    if (system(gzip_cmd) < 0) {
        syslog(LOG_ERR, "Failed to compress backup: %s", backup_file);
        return;
    }

    // Create a new log file
    int fd = open(log_file, O_CREAT | O_WRONLY | O_TRUNC, 0644);
    if (fd < 0) {
        syslog(LOG_ERR, "Failed to create new log file: %s", log_file);
        return;
    }
    close(fd);
}

// Clean up old backups
void clean_backups() {
    DIR *dir = opendir(BACKUP_DIR);
    if (!dir) {
        syslog(LOG_ERR, "Failed to open backup directory: %s", BACKUP_DIR);
        return;
    }

    struct dirent *entry;
    char backup_files[256][256];
    int count = 0;

    // Collect all backup files
    while ((entry = readdir(dir)) != NULL) {
        if (strstr(entry->d_name, ".gz")) {
            snprintf(backup_files[count], sizeof(backup_files[count]), "%s/%s", BACKUP_DIR, entry->d_name);
            count++;
        }
    }
    closedir(dir);

    // Sort backups by timestamp (simplified, assumes filename format: log.20240501...)
    for (int i = 0; i < count - 1; i++) {
        for (int j = i + 1; j < count; j++) {
            if (strcmp(backup_files[i], backup_files[j]) > 0) {
                char tmp[256];
                strcpy(tmp, backup_files[i]);
                strcpy(backup_files[i], backup_files[j]);
                strcpy(backup_files[j], tmp);
            }
        }
    }

    // Remove oldest backups beyond limit
    for (int i = 0; i < count - MAX_BACKUPS; i++) {
        if (unlink(backup_files[i]) < 0) {
            syslog(LOG_ERR, "Failed to remove old backup: %s", backup_files[i]);
        }
    }
}

// Handle signals
void signal_handler(int sig) {
    if (sig == SIGTERM) {
        syslog(LOG_INFO, "Shutting down log rotation daemon");
        closelog();
        exit(EXIT_SUCCESS);
    }
}

int main() {
    // Initialize syslog
    openlog("log_rotation_daemon", LOG_PID | LOG_DAEMON, LOG_USER);

    // Daemonize
    daemonize();

    // Set up signal handler
    signal(SIGTERM, signal_handler);

    while (1) {
        rotate_log();
        clean_backups();
        sleep(60); // Check every 60 seconds
    }

    closelog();
    return 0;
}
```

- **Backup Management**: Keeps at most `MAX_BACKUPS` compressed backups.
- **Signal Handling**: Gracefully handles `SIGTERM` to exit cleanly.
- **No External Dependencies**: Uses standard system tools like `gzip` for compression.

```c
#define BACKUP_DIR "/var/log/backups"
#define MAX_BACKUPS 5
#define MAX_SIZE (1024 * 1024 * 10)  // 10MB
#define SLEEP_INTERVAL 60            // Check every 60 seconds

void daemonize() {
    pid_t pid = fork();
    if (pid < 0) exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    if (pid > 0) exit(EXIT_SUCCESS);

    if (setsid() < 0) exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    pid = fork();
    if (pid < 0) exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    if (pid > 0) exit(EXIT_SUCCESS);

    umask(0);
    chdir("/");
    close(0);
    close(1);
    close(2);
}

void rotate_log() {
    struct stat st;
    if (stat(LOG_FILE, &st) != 0) return;

    if (st.st_size < MAX_SIZE) return;

    // Create backup name
    char backup[256];
    time_t now = time(NULL);
    strftime(backup, sizeof(backup), "%Y%m%d_%H%M%S", localtime(&now));
    snprintf(backup, sizeof(backup), "%s/%s.log", BACKUP_DIR, backup);

    // Rename and compress
    if (rename(LOG_FILE, backup) == 0) {
        char gzip_cmd[256];
        snprintf(gzip_cmd, sizeof(gzip_cmd), "gzip -f %s", backup);
        system(gzip_cmd);

    // Truncate the original log
    int fd = open(LOG_FILE, O_WRONLY | O_TRUNC | O_CREAT, 0644);
    if (fd >= 0) close(fd);

    char cmd[256];
    snprintf(cmd, sizeof(cmd), "cd %s && ls -t *.log.gz | tail -n +6 | xargs -I{} rm -f {}", BACKUP_DIR);
    system(cmd);
}

int main() {
    daemonize();

    while (1) {
        rotate_log();
        clean_backups();
        sleep(SLEEP_INTERVAL);
    }

    return 0;
```

```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <sys/stat.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <sys/types.h>
#include <errno.h>

#define LOG_FILE "app.log"
#define MAX_SIZE (1024 * 1024 * 10)  // 10MB
#define MAX_BACKUPS 5

void rotate_logs() {
    char old_log[256];
    char new_log[256];
    struct stat st;

    // Check if log file exists and is over the size limit
    if (stat(LOG_FILE, &st) == 0 && st.st_size >= MAX_SIZE) {
        // Shift existing backups up
        for (int i = MAX_BACKUPS - 1; i > 0; i--) {
            snprintf(old_log, sizeof(old_log), "%s.%d", LOG_FILE, i);
            snprintf(new_log, sizeof(new_log), "%s.%d", LOG_FILE, i + 1);

            // Skip if the file doesn't exist
            if (stat(old_log, &st) != 0) continue;

            if (rename(old_log, new_log) != 0) {
                perror("rename failed");
                continue;
            }
        }

        // Rename current log to log.1
        snprintf(old_log, sizeof(old_log), "%s", LOG_FILE);
        snprintf(new_log, sizeof(new_log), "%s.1", LOG_FILE);

        if (rename(old_log, new_log) != 0) {
            perror("rename failed");
            return;
        }

        // Truncate the original log to 0 size
        int fd = open(LOG_FILE, O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_TRUNC, 0644);
        if (fd != -1) {
            close(fd);
        } else {
            perror("open failed");
        }
    }
}

int main() {
    while (1) {
        rotate_logs();
        sleep(60); // Check every 60 seconds
    }

    return 0;
}
```

```c
    static struct timeval prev_time;
    struct timeval curr_time;
    double cpu_time = 0.0;

    gettimeofday(&curr_time, NULL);

    if (prev_time.tv_sec == 0 && prev_time.tv_usec == 0) {
        prev_time = curr_time;
        return 0.0;
    }

    double curr_usec = (curr_time.tv_sec * 1e6) + curr_time.tv_usec;
    double prev_usec = (prev_time.tv_sec * 1e6) + prev_time.tv_usec;

    cpu_time = (curr_usec - prev_usec) / 1e6;  // in seconds
    prev_time = curr_time;

    return cpu_time * 100.0 / sysconf(_SC_CLK_TCK);  // convert to percent
}
```

```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <pcap.h>
#include <netinet/ip.h>
#include <netinet/tcp.h>
#include <netinet/udp.h>
#include <arpa/inet.h>
#include <pthread.h>
#include <time.h>

#define MAX_FLOWS 100000
#define HASH_SIZE 1024

typedef struct {
    uint32_t src_ip;
    uint32_t dst_ip;
    uint16_t src_port;
    uint16_t dst_port;
    uint8_t protocol;
    uint64_t bytes;
    uint64_t packets;
    time_t last_seen;
} Flow;

typedef struct {
    Flow flow;
    struct FlowHashEntry* next;
} FlowHashEntry;

FlowHashEntry* flow_table[HASH_SIZE];

void hash_insert(Flow* flow) {
    unsigned int hash = (flow->src_ip ^ flow->dst_ip ^ flow->src_port ^ flow->dst_port) % HASH_SIZE;
    FlowHashEntry* entry = (FlowHashEntry*)malloc(sizeof(FlowHashEntry));
    entry->flow = *flow;
    entry->next = flow_table[hash];
    flow_table[hash] = entry;
}

FlowHashEntry* hash_lookup(uint32_t src_ip, uint16_t src_port, uint32_t dst_ip, uint16_t dst_port, uint8_t protocol) {
    unsigned int hash = (src_ip ^ dst_ip ^ src_port ^ dst_port) % HASH_SIZE;
    FlowHashEntry* entry = flow_table[hash];
    while (entry) {
        if (entry->flow.src_ip == src_ip &&
            entry->flow.dst_ip == dst_ip &&
            entry->flow.src_port == src_port &&
            entry->flow.dst_port == dst_port &&
            entry->flow.protocol == protocol) {
            return entry;
        }
        entry = entry->next;
    }
    return NULL;
}

void update_flow(FlowHashEntry* entry, uint32_t length) {
    entry->flow.bytes += length;
    entry->flow.packets++;
    entry->flow.last_seen = time(NULL);
}

void print_flows() {
    for (int i = 0; i < HASH_SIZE; i++) {
        FlowHashEntry* entry = flow_table[i];
        while (entry) {
            char src_ip[16], dst_ip[16];
            inet_ntop(AF_INET, &entry->flow.src_ip, src_ip, sizeof(src_ip));
            inet_ntop(AF_INET, &entry->flow.dst_ip, dst_ip, sizeof(dst_ip));
            printf("Flow: %s:%d -> %s:%d (Proto: %d) | Bytes: %lu | Packets: %lu | Last: %s\n",
                   src_ip, entry->flow.src_port, dst_ip, entry->flow.dst_port,
                   entry->flow.protocol, entry->flow.bytes, entry->flow.packets,
                   ctime(&entry->flow.last_seen));
            entry = entry->next;
        }
    }
}

void packet_handler(u_char* user, const struct pcap_pkthdr* pkthdr, const u_char* packet) {
    static int packet_count = 0;
    if (packet_count++ % 1000 == 0) {
        printf("Processing packet %d\n", packet_count);
    }

    const struct ip* ip_header = (struct ip*)(packet + 14); // Ethernet header is 14 bytes
    const uint8_t* transport_header = (uint8_t*)(packet + 14 + ip_header->ip_hl * 4);

    FlowHashEntry* entry = hash_lookup(ip_header->ip_src.s_addr, ntohs(((struct tcphdr*)transport_header)->th_sport),
                                       ip_header->ip_dst.s_addr, ntohs(((struct tcphdr*)transport_header)->th_dport),
                                       ip_header->ip_p);

    if (entry) {
        update_flow(entry, pkthdr->len);
    } else {
        Flow flow = {
            .src_ip = ip_header->ip_src.s_addr,
            .dst_ip = ip_header->ip_dst.s_addr,
            .src_port = ntohs(((struct tcphdr*)transport_header)->th_sport),
            .dst_port = ntohs(((struct tcphdr*)transport_header)->th_dport),
            .protocol = ip_header->ip_p,
            .bytes = pkthdr->len,
            .packets = 1,
            .last_seen = time(NULL)
        };
        hash_insert(&flow);
    }
}

void* monitor_thread(void* arg) {
    while (1) {
        sleep(10); // Periodically print flows
        print_flows();
    }
}

int main(int argc, char* argv[]) {
    char* dev = pcap_lookupdev(NULL);
    if (!dev) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Could not find default device\n");
        return 1;
    }

    char errbuf[PCAP_ERRBUF_SIZE];
    pcap_t* handle = pcap_open_live(dev, BUFSIZ, 1, 1000, errbuf);
    if (!handle) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Could not open device %s: %s\n", dev, errbuf);
        return 1;
    }

    pthread_t thread;
    pthread_create(&thread, NULL, monitor_thread, NULL);

    pcap_loop(handle, 0, packet_handler, NULL);

    pcap_close(handle);
    return 0;
}
```

```cpp
#include <iostream>
#include <unordered_map>
#include <mutex>
#include <thread>
#include <pcap/pcap.h>
#include <netinet/ip.h>
#include <netinet/tcp.h>
#include <arpa/inet.h>

struct FlowKey {
    std::string src_ip;
    std::string dst_ip;
    uint16_t src_port;
    uint16_t dst_port;

    bool operator==(const FlowKey& other) const {
        return src_ip == other.src_ip && dst_ip == other.dst_ip &&
               src_port == other.src_port && dst_port == other.dst_port;
    }
};

struct Flow {
    uint64_t bytes = 0;
    uint64_t packets = 0;
    uint64_t start_time = 0;
    uint64_t end_time = 0;
};

struct FlowHash {
    std::size_t operator()(const FlowKey& k) const {
        return std::hash<std::string>()(k.src_ip) ^ std::hash<std::string>()(k.dst_ip) ^
               std::hash<uint16_t>()(k.src_port) ^ std::hash<uint16_t>()(k.dst_port);
    }
};

std::unordered_map<FlowKey, Flow, FlowHash> flows;
std::mutex flow_mutex;

void packet_handler(u_char* user, const struct pcap_pkthdr* pkthdr, const u_char* packet) {
    const struct ether_header* eth_header = reinterpret_cast<const struct ether_header*>(packet);
    if (ntohs(eth_header->ether_type) != ETHERTYPE_IP) return;

    const struct ip* ip_header = reinterpret_cast<const struct ip*>(packet + sizeof(ether_header));
    if (ip_header->ip_p != IPPROTO_TCP) return;

    const struct tcphdr* tcp_header = reinterpret_cast<const struct tcphdr*>(packet + sizeof(ether_header) + sizeof(ip_header));
    const uint16_t src_port = ntohs(tcp_header->th_sport);
    const uint16_t dst_port = ntohs(tcp_header->th_dport);

    const char* src_ip = inet_ntoa(*(struct in_addr*)&ip_header->ip_src);
    const char* dst_ip = inet_ntoa(*(struct in_addr*)&ip_header->ip_dst);

    FlowKey key = {src_ip, dst_ip, src_port, dst_port};

    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(flow_mutex);
    auto it = flows.find(key);
    if (it == flows.end()) {
        flows[key] = {pkthdr->ts.tv_sec, 1, pkthdr->ts.tv_sec};
    } else {
        it->second.bytes += pkthdr->len;
        it->second.packets += 1;
        it->second.end_time = pkthdr->ts.tv_sec;
    }
}

void start_capture(const char* interface) {
    pcap_t* handle = pcap_open_live(interface, BUFSIZ, 1, 1000, nullptr);
    if (!handle) {
        std::cerr << "Could not open device " << interface << std::endl;
        return;
    }

    struct bpf_program fp;
    pcap_compile(handle, &fp, "tcp", 0, PCAP_NETMASK_UNKNOWN);
    pcap_setfilter(handle, &fp);

    pcap_loop(handle, -1, packet_handler, nullptr);
    pcap_close(handle);
}

int main(int argc, char* argv[]) {
    if (argc < 2) {
        std::cerr << "Usage: " << argv[0] << " <interface>" << std::endl;
        return 1;
    }

    std::thread capture_thread(start_capture, argv[1]);

    // Simulate a main loop to periodically print flows
    while (true) {
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::seconds(1));
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(flow_mutex);
        for (const auto& [key, flow] : flows) {
            std::cout << "Flow: " << key.src_ip << ":" << key.src_port << " -> " << key.dst_ip << ":" << key.dst_port
                      << " | Bytes: " << flow.bytes << " | Packets: " << flow.packets
                      << " | Duration: " << (flow.end_time - flow.start_time) << "s\n";
        }
    }

    capture_thread.join();
    return 0;
}
```

```cpp
    std::string src_ip;
    std::string dst_ip;
    uint16_t src_port;
    uint16_t dst_port;
    uint16_t protocol;
    uint64_t bytes;
    uint64_t packets;
};

void process_packet(u_char *user, const struct pcap_pkthdr *pkthdr, const u_char *packet) {
    const struct ether_header *eth = reinterpret_cast<const struct ether_header*>(packet);
    if (ntohs(eth->ether_type) != ETHERTYPE_IP) return;

    const struct ip *ip = reinterpret_cast<const struct ip*>(packet + sizeof(struct ether_header));
    uint16_t ip_len = ntohs(ip->ip_len);
    if (ip_len < sizeof(struct ip)) return;

    uint16_t ip_protocol = ip->ip_p;
    const u_char *transport_header = packet + sizeof(struct ether_header) + sizeof(struct ip);
    uint16_t transport_header_len = 0;
    uint16_t transport_protocol = 0;

    if (ip_protocol == IPPROTO_TCP) {
        const struct tcphdr *tcp = reinterpret_cast<const struct tcphdr*>(transport_header);
        transport_header_len = ntohs(tcp->th_off) * 4;
        transport_protocol = IPPROTO_TCP;
    } else if (ip_protocol == IPPROTO_UDP) {
        const struct udphdr *udp = reinterpret_cast<const struct udphdr*>(transport_header);
        transport_header_len = sizeof(struct udphdr);
        transport_protocol = IPPROTO_UDP;
    } else {
        return;
    }

    char src_ip[INET_ADDRSTRLEN], dst_ip[INET_ADDRSTRLEN];
    inet_ntop(AF_INET, &ip->ip_src, src_ip, INET_ADDRSTRLEN);
    inet_ntop(AF_INET, &ip->ip_dst, dst_ip, INET_ADDRSTRLEN);

    uint16_t src_port, dst_port;
    if (ip_protocol == IPPROTO_TCP) {
        const struct tcphdr *tcp = reinterpret_cast<const struct tcphdr*>(transport_header);
        src_port = ntohs(tcp->th_sport);
        dst_port = ntohs(tcp->th_dport);
    } else if (ip_protocol == IPPROTO_UDP) {
        const struct udphdr *udp = reinterpret_cast<const struct udphdr*>(transport_header);
        src_port = ntohs(udp->uh_sport);
        dst_port = ntohs(udp->uh_dport);
    }

    std::string key = src_ip + ":" + std::to_string(src_port) + "=>" + dst_ip + ":" + std::to_string(dst_port) + ":" + std::to_string(transport_protocol);

    static std::unordered_map<std::string, Flow> flows;
    auto it = flows.find(key);
    if (it != flows.end()) {
        it->second.bytes += pkthdr->caplen;
        it->second.packets++;
    } else {
        Flow flow;
        flow.src_ip = src_ip;
        flow.dst_ip = dst_ip;
        flow.src_port = src_port;
        flow.dst_port = dst_port;
        flow.protocol = transport_protocol;
        flow.bytes = pkthdr->caplen;
        flow.packets = 1;
        flows.insert({key, flow});
    }

    static int count = 0;
    count++;
    if (count % 1000 == 0) {
        for (const auto& [k, f] : flows) {
            std::cout << "Flow: " << k << " Bytes: " << f.bytes << " Packets: " << f.packets << std::endl;
        }
    }
}

int main(int argc, char *argv[]) {
    if (argc < 2) {
        std::cerr << "Usage: " << argv[0] << " <interface>" << std::endl;
        return 1;
    }

    char *device = argv[1];
    char errbuf[PCAP_ERRBUF_SIZE];
    pcap_t *handle = pcap_open_live(device, BUFSIZ, 1, 1000, errbuf);
    if (!handle) {
        std::cerr << "Couldn't open device " << device << ": " << errbuf << std::endl;
        return 1;
    }

    struct bpf_program fp;
    if (pcap_compile(handle, &fp, "ip", 0, PCAP_NETMASK_UNKNOWN) == -1) {
        std::cerr << "Couldn't parse filter: " << pcap_geterr(handle) << std::endl;
        return 1;
    }
    if (pcap_setfilter(handle, &fp) == -1) {
        std::cerr << "Couldn't install filter: " << pcap_geterr(handle) << std::endl;
        return 1;
    }

    pcap_loop(handle, 0, process_packet, nullptr);

    pcap_close(handle);
    return 0;
}
```

```c
}

    struct iphdr ip_header;

        struct tcphdr tcp_header;
        int ip_header_len = ip_header.ihl * 4;
```

```c
#include <stdio.h>

// Define a structure for a flow
typedef struct {
    char src_ip[16];
    char dst_ip[16];
    uint16_t src_port;
    uint16_t dst_port;
    uint64_t bytes;
    uint64_t packets;
} Flow;

// Define a hash table entry (open addressing with chaining)
typedef struct {
    Flow flow;
    struct HashEntry* next;
} HashEntry;

// Hash table structure
typedef struct {
    HashEntry** buckets;
    size_t size;
} HashTable;

// Simple hash function
unsigned int hash(const char* ip, uint16_t port) {
    unsigned int h = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < strlen(ip); i++) {
        h = (h * 31) + ip[i];
    }
    h += port;
    return h % 1024; // Size of hash table
}

// Initialize hash table
HashTable* create_hash_table(size_t size) {
    HashTable* table = (HashTable*)malloc(sizeof(HashTable));
    table->size = size;
    table->buckets = (HashEntry**)calloc(size, sizeof(HashEntry*));
    return table;
}

// Add a flow to the hash table
void add_flow(HashTable* table, Flow* flow) {
    unsigned int index = hash(flow->src_ip, flow->src_port);
    HashEntry* entry = (HashEntry*)malloc(sizeof(HashEntry));
    entry->flow = *flow;
    entry->next = table->buckets[index];
    table->buckets[index] = entry;
}

// Find a flow in the hash table
Flow* find_flow(HashTable* table, const char* src_ip, uint16_t src_port, const char* dst_ip, uint16_t dst_port) {
    unsigned int index = hash(src_ip, src_port);
    HashEntry* entry = table->buckets[index];
    while (entry != NULL) {
        if (strcmp(entry->flow.src_ip, src_ip) == 0 &&
            entry->flow.src_port == src_port &&
            strcmp(entry->flow.dst_ip, dst_ip) == 0 &&
            entry->flow.dst_port == dst_port) {
            return &entry->flow;
        }
        entry = entry->next;
    }
    return NULL;
}

// Print all flows in the hash table
void print_flows(HashTable* table) {
    for (size_t i = 0; i < table->size; i++) {
        HashEntry* entry = table->buckets[i];
        while (entry != NULL) {
            printf("Flow: %s:%d -> %s:%d | Bytes: %llu | Packets: %llu\n",
                   entry->flow.src_ip, entry->flow.src_port,
                   entry->flow.dst_ip, entry->flow.dst_port,
                   entry->flow.bytes, entry->flow.packets);
            entry = entry->next;
        }
    }
}

    static time_t last_print = 0;

    const struct ether_header* eth_hdr = (struct ether_header*)packet;
    if (ntohs(eth_hdr->ether_type) != ETHERTYPE_IP) {
        return; // Not IP traffic

    if (ip_hdr->ip_v != 4) {
        return; // Not IPv4

    if (ip_hdr->ip_p == IPPROTO_TCP) {
        transport_hdr = packet + sizeof(struct ether_header) + ip_hdr->ip_hl * 4;
        transport_hdr_len = sizeof(struct tcphdr);
    } else if (ip_hdr->ip_p == IPPROTO_UDP) {
        transport_hdr = packet + sizeof(struct ether_header) + ip_hdr->ip_hl * 4;
        transport_hdr_len = sizeof(struct udphdr);
    } else {
        return; // Not TCP/UDP
    }

    // Extract source and destination ports
    uint16_t src_port, dst_port;
    if (ip_hdr->ip_p == IPPROTO_TCP) {
        const struct tcphdr* tcp_hdr = (struct tcphdr*)transport_hdr;
        src_port = ntohs(tcp_hdr->th_sport);
        dst_port = ntohs(tcp_hdr->th_dport);
    } else {
        const struct udphdr* udp_hdr = (struct udphdr*)transport_hdr;
        src_port = ntohs(udp_hdr->uh_sport);
        dst_port = ntohs(udp_hdr->uh_dport);
    }

    // Convert IP addresses to strings
    char src_ip[16], dst_ip[16];
    inet_ntop(AF_INET, &ip_hdr->ip_src, src_ip, sizeof(src_ip));
    inet_ntop(AF_INET, &ip_hdr->ip_dst, dst_ip, sizeof(dst_ip));

    // Find or create the flow
    Flow* flow = find_flow(table, src_ip, src_port, dst_ip, dst_port);
    if (flow == NULL) {
        Flow new_flow;
        strcpy(new_flow.src_ip, src_ip);
        strcpy(new_flow.dst_ip, dst_ip);
        new_flow.src_port = src_port;
        new_flow.dst_port = dst_port;
        new_flow.bytes = 0;
        new_flow.packets = 0;
        add_flow(table, &new_flow);
        flow = find_flow(table, src_ip, src_port, dst_ip, dst_port);
    }

    // Update the flow statistics
    flow->bytes += pkthdr->len;
    flow->packets += 1;

    // Print flows every 5 seconds

        last_print = now;
```

```c
        uint16_t raw_value = read_sensor();
        uint16_t processed_value = process_data(raw_value);
        output_result(processed_value);

    }

    return 0;

    ADMUX = (1 << REFS0) | (SENSOR_PIN & 0x07);  // Set reference voltage and channel
    ADCSRA = (1 << ADEN) | (1 << ADPS2) | (1 << ADPS1) | (1 << ADPS0);  // Enable ADC, set prescaler
}

// Read raw sensor value from ADC
uint16_t read_sensor(void) {
    uint16_t sum = 0;
    for (uint8_t i = 0; i < SAMPLES; i++) {
        ADCSRA |= (1 << ADSC);  // Start conversion
        while (ADCSRA & (1 << ADSC));  // Wait for conversion to complete
        sum += ADC;  // Read result from ADC register
    }
    return sum / SAMPLES;  // Return average of samples
}

    if (raw_value > THRESHOLD) {
        return 1;  // Signal: threshold exceeded

    }
}

// Output processed result (example: toggle LED or send via UART)

}
```

```c
#define SAMPLE_COUNT 10 // Number of samples to average
```

```cpp
    Eigen::VectorXd update(const Eigen::VectorXd& measurement) {
        // Predict step

        P_ = A_ * P_ * A_.transpose() + Q_;

        Eigen::MatrixXd S = H_ * P_ * H_.transpose() + R_;
        Eigen::MatrixXd K = P_ * H_.transpose() * S.inverse();
        x_ = x_ + K * y;
```

```cpp
        fused.linear_velocity = 0.8 * imu_data.linear_velocity + 0.2 * encoder_data.linear_velocity;
        fused.angular_velocity = 0.8 * imu_data.angular_velocity + 0.2 * encoder_data.angular_velocity;
        fused.encoder_position = encoder_data.encoder_position;
        fused.imu_angle = imu_data.imu_angle;
```

```c
float read_sensor_data() {
    // Simulate normal data with occasional anomalies
    static int sample_index = 0;
    float data[] = {1.0, 1.1, 0.9, 1.0, 1.2, 0.95, 1.05, 1.0, 1.0, 1.1};
    sample_index = (sample_index + 1) % sizeof(data) / sizeof(data[0]);
    return data[sample_index];
}

// Simple anomaly detection based on deviation from a moving average
bool detect_anomaly(float* buffer, int buffer_size) {
    float sum = 0.0f;
    for (int i = 0; i < buffer_size; i++) {
        sum += buffer[i];
    }
    float mean = sum / buffer_size;
    float deviation = 0.0f;
    for (int i = 0; i < buffer_size; i++) {
        deviation += pow(buffer[i] - mean, 2.0);
    }
    float std_dev = sqrt(deviation / buffer_size);

    // Anomaly if data point exceeds mean + threshold * standard deviation
    for (int i = 0; i < buffer_size; i++) {
        if (fabs(buffer[i] - mean) > ANOMALY_THRESHOLD * std_dev) {
            return true;
        }
    }
    return false;
}

int main() {
    float buffer[BUFFER_SIZE];
    int buffer_index = 0;

    while (1) {
        // Read sensor data
        float data = read_sensor_data();

        // Store data in buffer
        buffer[buffer_index++] = data;
        if (buffer_index >= BUFFER_SIZE) {
            buffer_index = 0;
        }

        // Check for anomaly
        if (detect_anomaly(buffer, BUFFER_SIZE)) {
            printf("Anomaly detected!\n");
        }

        // Simulate a short delay (replace with real-time timing in embedded systems)
        for (volatile int i = 0; i < 1000000; i++);
    }

    return 0;
}
```

```c
    uint32_t index;
    float sum;
} MovingAverage;

// Initialize moving average buffer
void moving_average_init(MovingAverage *ma) {
    memset(ma->buffer, 0, sizeof(ma->buffer));
    ma->index = 0;
    ma->sum = 0.0f;
}

// Add a new sample to the moving average
void moving_average_add(MovingAverage *ma, float value) {
    if (ma->index >= WINDOW_SIZE) {
        ma->index = 0; // Wrap around if buffer is full
    }

    float old_value = ma->buffer[ma->index];
    ma->sum = ma->sum - old_value + value;
    ma->buffer[ma->index++] = value;
}

// Calculate standard deviation of the buffer
float moving_average_stddev(MovingAverage *ma) {
    if (ma->index == 0) {
        return 0.0f; // No data yet
    }

    float mean = ma->sum / (float)WINDOW_SIZE;
    float variance = 0.0f;

    for (int i = 0; i < WINDOW_SIZE; i++) {
        float diff = ma->buffer[i] - mean;
        variance += diff * diff;
    }

    return sqrtf(variance / (float)WINDOW_SIZE);
```

```c
    noise += (rand() % 100 - 50) * 0.001f;  // Add small random noise
    return (AccelerometerData) {
        .x = baseline_x + noise,
        .y = baseline_y + noise,
        .z = baseline_z + noise
    };
}

// Calculate the average of the last N samples
float calculate_average(float samples[SAMPLE_BUFFER_SIZE]) {
    float sum = 0.0f;
    for (int i = 0; i < SAMPLE_BUFFER_SIZE; i++) {
        sum += samples[i];
    }
    return sum / SAMPLE_BUFFER_SIZE;
}

// Detect anomalies using a simple threshold-based method
int detect_anomaly(AccelerometerData sample) {
    static float x_history[SAMPLE_BUFFER_SIZE];
    static float y_history[SAMPLE_BUFFER_SIZE];
    static float z_history[SAMPLE_BUFFER_SIZE];

    x_history[buffer_index] = sample.x;
    y_history[buffer_index] = sample.y;
    z_history[buffer_index] = sample.z;
    buffer_index = (buffer_index + 1) % SAMPLE_BUFFER_SIZE;

    // Calculate average for each axis
    float avg_x = calculate_average(x_history);
    float avg_y = calculate_average(y_history);
    float avg_z = calculate_average(z_history);

    // Detect anomalies if any axis deviates by more than the threshold
    if (fabs(sample.x - avg_x) > THRESHOLD ||
        fabs(sample.y - avg_y) > THRESHOLD ||
        fabs(sample.z - avg_z) > THRESHOLD) {
        return 1;  // Anomaly detected
    }
    return 0;  // No anomaly
```

```c
typedef struct {
    uint16_t buffer[FILTER_WINDOW_SIZE];
    uint16_t index;
    uint16_t sum;

    filter->index = 0;
    filter->sum = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < FILTER_WINDOW_SIZE; i++) {

    }
```

```cpp
    Actuator actuator;

    const float threshold = 110.0f;

        }
        filteredValue /= bufferLength;

            filterAndControl();
            std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(100)); // Simulate periodic sampling
```

Here's a minimal working 2D platformer game using **Python** with **Pygame**, featuring basic physics simulation (gravity, jumping) and sprite animation. This example assumes you have Pygame installed (`pip install pygame`). Save the code as `platformer.py` and run it.

---

### 🎮 Minimal 2D Platformer Game (Python + Pygame)

```python
import pygame
import sys

# Initialize Pygame
pygame.init()

# Screen settings
WIDTH, HEIGHT = 800, 600
screen = pygame.display.set_mode((WIDTH, HEIGHT))
pygame.display.set_caption("Minimal 2D Platformer")

# Colors
WHITE = (255, 255, 255)
BLUE = (0, 0, 255)
GREEN = (0, 255, 0)

# Game clock
clock = pygame.time.Clock()
FPS = 60

# Player class
class Player(pygame.sprite.Sprite):
    def __init__(self, x, y):
        super().__init__()
        self.width, self.height = 50, 50
        self.image = pygame.Surface((self.width, self.height))
        self.image.fill(BLUE)
        self.rect = self.image.get_rect(topleft=(x, y))
        self.vel_y = 0
        self.on_ground = False
        self.animation_frame = 0
        self.sprites = [pygame.Surface((self.width, self.height)) for _ in range(4)]
        for i, surf in enumerate(self.sprites):
            surf.fill((255, 0, i * 60))  # Simulated animation frames

    def update(self, platforms):
        # Gravity
        self.vel_y += 1
        if self.vel_y > 10:
            self.vel_y = 10
        self.rect.y += self.vel_y

        # Collision with platforms
        self.on_ground = False
        for platform in platforms:
            if self.rect.colliderect(platform.rect):
                if self.vel_y > 0:
                    self.rect.bottom = platform.rect.top
                    self.vel_y = 0
                    self.on_ground = True

        # Horizontal movement
        keys = pygame.key.get_pressed()
        if keys[pygame.K_LEFT]:
            self.rect.x -= 5
        if keys[pygame.K_RIGHT]:
            self.rect.x += 5
        if keys[pygame.K_SPACE] and self.on_ground:
            self.vel_y = -15

        # Animation
        self.animation_frame = (self.animation_frame + 1) % len(self.sprites)
        self.image = self.sprites[self.animation_frame]

# Platform class
class Platform(pygame.sprite.Sprite):
    def __init__(self, x, y, width, height):
        super().__init__()
        self.image = pygame.Surface((width, height))
        self.image.fill(GREEN)
        self.rect = self.image.get_rect(topleft=(x, y))

# Create groups
all_sprites = pygame.sprite.Group()
platforms = pygame.sprite.Group()

# Create player
player = Player(100, 100)
all_sprites.add(player)

# Create platforms
ground = Platform(0, HEIGHT - 40, WIDTH, 40)
platform = Platform(300, 400, 200, 20)
platforms.add(ground, platform)
all_sprites.add(ground, platform)

# Game loop
while True:
    for event in pygame.event.get():
        if event.type == pygame.QUIT:
            pygame.quit()
            sys.exit()

    all_sprites.update(platforms)

    # Drawing
    screen.fill(WHITE)
    all_sprites.draw(screen)
    pygame.display.flip()
    clock.tick(FPS)
```

---

### 🔧 Features Implemented

1. **Physics Simulation**:
   - Gravity: `self.vel_y += 1`
   - Jumping: `self.vel_y = -15` when spacebar is pressed and on the ground.
   - Collision detection with platforms.

2. **Sprite Animation**:
   - Simulated with 4 color-changing frames (`self.sprites`).
   - Animation cycles via `self.animation_frame`.

3. **Controls**:
   - Left/Right movement with arrow keys.
   - Jump with the spacebar.

---

### 🧪 How to Run
1. Install Pygame:  
   ```bash
   pip install pygame
   ```
2. Save the code as `platformer.py`.
3. Run it:  
   ```bash
   python platformer.py
   ```

- This is a **minimal** example for illustration. Real games would include:
  - Tilemaps or level editors.
  - Sound effects and music.
  - More sophisticated animations (e.g., using sprite sheets).
  - Collision resolution for slopes and moving platforms.

Here's a **minimal working example** of a 2D platformer game with **physics simulation** (gravity and collision) and **sprite animation** using **Python** and **Pygame**. This example assumes you have a sprite sheet for the player (e.g., 2 frames for walking). Replace `player_sprite.png` with your own sprite sheet.

---

### 🕹️ Minimal 2D Platformer Game (Python + Pygame)

```python
import pygame
import sys

# Initialize Pygame
pygame.init()

# Constants
WIDTH, HEIGHT = 800, 600
FPS = 60
GRAVITY = 0.5
PLAYER_SPEED = 5
JUMP_STRENGTH = -10

# Setup
screen = pygame.display.set_mode((WIDTH, HEIGHT))
clock = pygame.time.Clock()

# Load assets
player_image = pygame.image.load("player_sprite.png")  # Replace with your sprite sheet
player_rect = player_image.get_rect()
player_rect.center = (100, 100)

# Sprite animation (2 frames)
frame_width = player_image.get_width() // 2
current_frame = 0

# Platforms
platforms = [
    pygame.Rect(100, 500, 200, 20),
    pygame.Rect(400, 400, 200, 20),
    pygame.Rect(600, 300, 200, 20),
]

# Player physics
player_velocity = [0, 0]
on_ground = False

# Game loop
while True:
    for event in pygame.event.get():
        if event.type == pygame.QUIT:
            pygame.quit()
            sys.exit()

    # Input
    keys = pygame.key.get_pressed()
    player_velocity[0] = 0
    if keys[pygame.K_LEFT]:
        player_velocity[0] = -PLAYER_SPEED
        current_frame = 0
    elif keys[pygame.K_RIGHT]:
        player_velocity[0] = PLAYER_SPEED
        current_frame = 1
    else:
        current_frame = 0  # Idle frame (you can add more frames)

    # Jump
    if keys[pygame.K_SPACE] and on_ground:
        player_velocity[1] = JUMP_STRENGTH
        on_ground = False

    # Apply gravity
    player_velocity[1] += GRAVITY

    # Move player
    player_rect.x += player_velocity[0]
    player_rect.y += player_velocity[1]

    # Collision with platforms
    on_ground = False
    for platform in platforms:
        if player_rect.colliderect(platform):
            if player_velocity[1] > 0:  # Falling down
                player_rect.bottom = platform.top
                player_velocity[1] = 0
                on_ground = True
            elif player_velocity[1] < 0:  # Jumping up
                player_rect.top = platform.bottom
                player_velocity[1] = 0

    # Wrap around screen edges
    if player_rect.left < 0:
        player_rect.left = 0
    if player_rect.right > WIDTH:
        player_rect.right = WIDTH

    # Draw
    screen.fill((135, 206, 250))  # Sky blue background
    for platform in platforms:
        pygame.draw.rect(screen, (0, 128, 0), platform)  # Green platforms

    # Sprite animation
    frame_rect = pygame.Rect(current_frame * frame_width, 0, frame_width, player_image.get_height())
    screen.blit(player_image, player_rect, frame_rect)

    pygame.display.flip()
    clock.tick(FPS)
```

---

### 🔍 Key Features Implemented:
1. **Physics Simulation**:
   - Gravity (`GRAVITY`) pulls the player down.
   - Collision detection with platforms (simple AABB).
   - Jumping with `JUMP_STRENGTH` when on the ground.

**Minimal 2D Platformer Example**:  
This example uses Godot's built-in physics, sprite animation, and node system to create a basic 2D platformer.  

---

### **Steps to Set Up in Godot**  
1. **Create a New Project**: Open Godot, create a new 2D project.  
2. **Add a Player Node**:  
   - Add a `KinematicBody2D` node as the root.  
   - Add a `Sprite` node as a child (load a player sprite, e.g., a red square).  
   - Add an `AnimationPlayer` node as a child (create idle and run animations).  
   - Add a `CollisionShape2D` node with a `RectangleShape2D` for collision.  

3. **Add Platforms**:  
   - Create `StaticBody2D` nodes with `CollisionShape2D` for platforms.  

4. **Attach Script to Player**:  

```gdscript
extends KinematicBody2D

var velocity = Vector2()
var gravity = 500
var jump_force = -300
var speed = 200
var on_ground = false

func _physics_process(delta):
    var input = Input.get_action_strength("ui_right") - Input.get_action_strength("ui_left")
    velocity.x = input * speed

    # Apply gravity
    velocity.y += gravity * delta

    # Check for ground collision
    var ground_mask = 1 << 1  # Assuming platforms are in layer 1
    var ground = get_slide_collision(0)
    on_ground = ground.collider.is_in_group("platforms")

    # Jump
    if Input.is_action_just_pressed("ui_jump") and on_ground:
        velocity.y = jump_force

    # Move
    velocity = move_and_slide(velocity, Vector2.UP)

    # Play animation
    if input != 0:
        $AnimationPlayer.play("run")
    else:
        $AnimationPlayer.play("idle")
```

---

### **Explanation**  
- **Physics**: Uses `KinematicBody2D` and `move_and_slide()` for physics simulation.  
- **Animation**: `AnimationPlayer` handles idle and run animations based on input.  
- **Collision**: Checks for collisions with platforms using `get_slide_collision()`.  

---

### **Requirements**  
- **Sprites**: Replace the placeholder sprite with your own.  
- **Animations**: Create "idle" and "run" animations in the `AnimationPlayer`.  
- **Groups**: Assign platforms to the "platforms" group in the `StaticBody2D` nodes.  

---

### **Why GDScript/ Godot?**  
- **Built-in 2D Tools**: No need for external physics libraries.  
- **Node-Based Architecture**: Simplifies scene management.  
- **Open Source**: Free and beginner-friendly.

responses:
<language>JavaScript</language>

Here's a **basic real-time 3D scene viewer** using **Three.js**, a powerful WebGL library for rendering 3D graphics in the browser. This example includes **dynamic lighting** and a **custom shader effect** (e.g., glowing colors based on light intensity). You can run this in an HTML file with a CDN link to Three.js.

---

### ✅ Code: Real-Time 3D Scene Viewer with Dynamic Lighting and Shader Effects

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <title>3D Scene Viewer</title>
  <style>
    body { margin: 0; overflow: hidden; }
    canvas { display: block; }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <!-- Include Three.js from CDN -->
  <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.157.0/build/three.min.js"></script>
  <script>
    // Scene, Camera, Renderer
    const scene = new THREE.Scene();
    const camera = new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(75, window.innerWidth / window.innerHeight, 0.1, 1000);
    const renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ antialias: true });
    renderer.setSize(window.innerWidth, window.innerHeight);
    document.body.appendChild(renderer.domElement);

    // Lighting
    const ambientLight = new THREE.AmbientLight(0xffffff, 0.4);
    scene.add(ambientLight);

    const pointLight = new THREE.PointLight(0xffffff, 1);
    pointLight.position.set(5, 5, 5);
    scene.add(pointLight);

    // Geometry and Material with Shader
    const geometry = new THREE.SphereGeometry(1, 32, 32);
    const material = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({
      color: 0x00ffcc,
      metalness: 0.5,
      roughness: 0.3,
      // Custom shader using fragment shader (simplified)
      fragmentShader: `
        varying vec2 vUv;
        void main() {
          vec3 lightDir = normalize(vec3(0.5, 0.5, 0.5));
          float intensity = max(0.0, dot(normalize(vNormal), lightDir));
          vec3 color = vec3(0.0, 1.0, 1.0) * intensity * 2.0;
          gl_FragColor = vec4(color, 1.0);
        }
      `,
      vertexShader: `
        varying vec2 vUv;
        varying vec3 vNormal;
        void main() {
          vUv = uv;
          vNormal = normal;
          gl_Position = projectionMatrix * modelViewMatrix * vec4(position, 1.0);
        }
      `
    });

    const sphere = new THREE.Mesh(geometry, material);
    scene.add(sphere);

    // Camera Position
    camera.position.z = 3;

    // Animation Loop
    function animate() {
      requestAnimationFrame(animate);

      // Dynamic Light Movement
      pointLight.position.x = Math.sin(Date.now() * 0.002) * 5;
      pointLight.position.y = Math.cos(Date.now() * 0.002) * 5;

      renderer.render(scene, camera);
    }

    animate();

    // Handle window resize
    window.addEventListener('resize', () => {
      camera.aspect = window.innerWidth / window.innerHeight;
      camera.updateProjectionMatrix();
      renderer.setSize(window.innerWidth, window.innerHeight);
    });
  </script>
</body>
</html>
```

---

### 🔍 Features Implemented:

1. **Dynamic Lighting**:
   - A `PointLight` moves in a circular path around the sphere, creating a glowing, animated effect.

### 🔧 **Custom Physics Plugin Example (C++)**

```cpp
    virtual void ApplyForce(RigidBody* body, const Vector3& force) = 0;

// Rigid Body Component
// ---------------------------
class RigidBody {
public:
    RigidBody() : position(0.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f), velocity(0.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f), mass(1.0f) {}

    Vector3 position;
    Vector3 velocity;
    float mass;

    // Example: Apply force and update velocity
    void ApplyForce(const Vector3& force, float deltaTime) {
        velocity += force / mass * deltaTime;
    }

    // Example: Integrate position based on velocity
    void IntegratePosition(float deltaTime) {
        position += velocity * deltaTime;
    }
};

// ---------------------------
// Collision Detection Utility
// ---------------------------
class CollisionDetection {
public:
    static bool CheckCollision(RigidBody* a, RigidBody* b) {

};

// ---------------------------
class CustomPhysicsSystem : public PhysicsSystem {
public:
    void Update(float deltaTime) override {
        for (auto body : rigidBodies) {
            // Apply gravity
            body->ApplyForce(Vector3(0.0f, -9.81f * body->mass, 0.0f), deltaTime);

            // Integrate position
            body->IntegratePosition(deltaTime);

            // Collision checks (simplified)

                    // Handle collision (e.g., apply impulse, resolve penetration)
                    std::cout << "Collision detected between bodies!" << std::endl;
                }
            }
        }
    }

    void AddRigidBody(RigidBody* body) override {
        rigidBodies.push_back(body);
    }

    void RemoveRigidBody(RigidBody* body) override {
        rigidBodies.erase(std::remove(rigidBodies.begin(), rigidBodies.end(), body), rigidBodies.end());
    }

        body->ApplyForce(force, 0.016f); // Assuming 60 FPS
    }

private:

};

// Example: Attach physics system to a game object
class PhysicsPlugin {
public:
    PhysicsPlugin() {
        physicsSystem = new CustomPhysicsSystem();
    }

    void Initialize(Engine::GameObject* gameObject) {
        // Register this plugin with the engine
        gameObject->AddComponent(physicsSystem);
    }
```

3. **`CustomPhysicsSystem` Class**:

4. **`PhysicsPlugin` Class**:
   - Acts as a bridge between the plugin and the game engine.
   - Registers the physics system with the engine's object system.

- **Engine-Specific APIs**: Replace `Engine::GameObject`, `Engine::Transform`, etc., with the actual types used by your target engine (e.g., Unity’s `GameObject`, Unreal’s `UActor`).

- **Memory Management**: Ensure proper ownership and cleanup of physics objects to avoid leaks.

Here's a simplified initial implementation of a custom physics plugin for a commercial game engine, focusing on basic rigid-body dynamics and collision detection. This example assumes integration with a game engine that supports C++ plugins (e.g., Unreal Engine, Unity via native plugins, or a custom engine).

---

### **Header File: `PhysicsPlugin.h`**
```cpp
#pragma once

#include <vector>
#include <cmath>

// Forward declaration for the engine's Vector3 type
struct Vector3 {
    float x, y, z;
};

// Rigid body representation
struct RigidBody {
    Vector3 position;
    Vector3 velocity;
    float mass;
    bool isStatic;

    RigidBody(Vector3 pos, float mass, bool isStatic = false)
        : position(pos), velocity{0, 0, 0}, mass(mass), isStatic(isStatic) {}
};

// Physics system interface
class PhysicsSystem {
public:
    PhysicsSystem();
    ~PhysicsSystem();

    void Initialize();
    void Update(float deltaTime);
    void AddBody(RigidBody* body);
    void CheckCollisions();

private:
    std::vector<RigidBody*> bodies;
    void ApplyGravity(float deltaTime);
    void ResolveCollision(RigidBody* a, RigidBody* b);
};
```

---

### **Source File: `PhysicsPlugin.cpp`**
```cpp
#include "PhysicsPlugin.h"
#include <iostream>

PhysicsSystem::PhysicsSystem() {
    Initialize();
}

PhysicsSystem::~PhysicsSystem() {
    for (auto body : bodies) {
        delete body;
    }
}

void PhysicsSystem::Initialize() {
    // Initialize physics system (e.g., gravity, collision shapes)
    std::cout << "Physics plugin initialized." << std::endl;
}

void PhysicsSystem::Update(float deltaTime) {
    ApplyGravity(deltaTime);
    CheckCollisions();
}

void PhysicsSystem::AddBody(RigidBody* body) {
    bodies.push_back(body);
}

void PhysicsSystem::ApplyGravity(float deltaTime) {
    for (auto body : bodies) {
        if (!body->isStatic) {
            body->velocity.y -= 9.81f * deltaTime; // Simulate gravity
            body->position.x += body->velocity.x * deltaTime;
            body->position.z += body->velocity.z * deltaTime;
            body->position.y += body->velocity.y * deltaTime;
        }
    }
}

void PhysicsSystem::CheckCollisions() {
    for (size_t i = 0; i < bodies.size(); ++i) {
        for (size_t j = i + 1; j < bodies.size(); ++j) {
            RigidBody* a = bodies[i];
            RigidBody* b = bodies[j];

            // Simple AABB collision detection (for demonstration)
            bool collision = (a->position.x < b->position.x + 1.0f &&
                              a->position.x + 1.0f > b->position.x &&
                              a->position.z < b->position.z + 1.0f &&
                              a->position.z + 1.0f > b->position.z);

            if (collision) {
                ResolveCollision(a, b);
            }
        }
    }
}

void PhysicsSystem::ResolveCollision(RigidBody* a, RigidBody* b) {
    // Simple elastic collision resolution
    float massA = a->mass;
    float massB = b->mass;

    Vector3 velocityA = a->velocity;
    Vector3 velocityB = b->velocity;

    // Swap velocities for simplicity (basic elastic collision)
    a->velocity = velocityB;
    b->velocity = velocityA;

    std::cout << "Collision detected between bodies!" << std::endl;
}
```

Here's a basic implementation of a **custom physics plugin** in **C++**, designed for integration into a commercial game engine (e.g., Unreal Engine, custom engine, or a plugin system like Unity's Native Plugins). This example includes a simple rigid-body physics system with gravity and collision detection.

---

### 🧱 **Core Physics Plugin Implementation**

```cpp
#include <vector>
#include <cmath>
#include <iostream>

// Forward declaration for collision detection
struct AABB;
struct RigidBody;

// Axis-Aligned Bounding Box (AABB) for collision detection
struct AABB {
    float min_x, min_y, min_z;
    float max_x, max_y, max_z;

    AABB(float x, float y, float z, float size)
        : min_x(x - size), min_y(y - size), min_z(z - size),
          max_x(x + size), max_y(y + size), max_z(z + size) {}

    bool Intersects(const AABB& other) const {
        return (min_x < other.max_x && max_x > other.min_x &&
                min_y < other.max_y && max_y > other.min_y &&
                min_z < other.max_z && max_z > other.min_z);
    }
};

// Rigid body with position, velocity, and mass
struct RigidBody {
    float position_x, position_y, position_z;
    float velocity_x, velocity_y, velocity_z;
    float mass;
    AABB aabb;

    RigidBody(float x, float y, float z, float mass, float size)
        : position_x(x), position_y(y), position_z(z),
          velocity_x(0.0f), velocity_y(0.0f), velocity_z(0.0f),
          mass(mass), aabb(x, y, z, size) {}

    void ApplyForce(float fx, float fy, float fz) {
        velocity_x += fx / mass * 0.016f; // Time step (approx 60 FPS)
        velocity_y += fy / mass * 0.016f;
        velocity_z += fz / mass * 0.016f;
    }

    void UpdatePosition() {
        position_x += velocity_x * 0.016f;
        position_y += velocity_y * 0.016f;
        position_z += velocity_z * 0.016f;
    }

    void ApplyGravity(float gravity) {
        ApplyForce(0.0f, -gravity * mass, 0.0f);
    }

    void ResolveCollision(RigidBody& other) {
        // Simple velocity swap for elastic collision
        std::swap(velocity_x, other.velocity_x);
        std::swap(velocity_y, other.velocity_y);
        std::swap(velocity_z, other.velocity_z);
    }
};

// Physics system manager
class PhysicsSystem {
public:
    static void UpdatePhysics(std::vector<RigidBody*>& bodies) {
        for (auto body : bodies) {
            body->ApplyGravity(9.81f); // Earth gravity
            body->UpdatePosition();
        }

        // Collision detection
        for (size_t i = 0; i < bodies.size(); ++i) {
            for (size_t j = i + 1; j < bodies.size(); ++j) {
                if (bodies[i]->aabb.Intersects(bodies[j]->aabb)) {
                    bodies[i]->ResolveCollision(*bodies[j]);
                }
            }
        }
    }
};
```

---

### 🛠️ **Integration with a Game Engine**

1. **Compile as a Shared Library**  
   - Compile the code into a `.dll` (Windows) or `.so` (Linux) for integration with the game engine.  
   - Example:  
     ```bash
     g++ -shared -fPIC -o physics_plugin.so physics_plugin.cpp
     ```

2. **Expose API for Engine Integration**  
   - Use `extern "C"` to export functions for the engine to call.  
   - Example:  
     ```cpp
     extern "C" {
         void UpdatePhysicsPlugin(void* bodies, int count) {
             std::vector<RigidBody*> bodies_vector = reinterpret_cast<std::vector<RigidBody*>>(bodies);
             PhysicsSystem::UpdatePhysics(bodies_vector);
         }
     }
     ```

3. **Engine-Specific Setup**  
   - For **Unreal Engine**, use the **Plugin Manager** to load the `.dll` and bind the `UpdatePhysicsPlugin` function.  
   - For **Unity**, use **Native Plugins** with `DllImport` to call the C++ functions.

---

### 📌 **Limitations of This Example**
- **Simplistic Physics**: Uses Euler integration and basic AABB collision. Real engines require more advanced solvers (e.g., impulse-based, constraint-based).
- **No Constraints**: No joints, springs, or rigid-body constraints.
- **No Broad-Phase Optimization**: Collision detection is brute-force (O(n²)), which is inefficient for large systems.

---

### 🚀 **Next Steps for a Commercial Plugin**
1. **Add Constraints** (e.g., hinges, springs).
2. **Use SIMD/AVX** for performance.
3. **Integrate with the Engine's Physics System** (e.g., replace or extend existing components).
4. **Add Debug Visualization** (e.g., draw AABBs in the engine's viewport).

Here's a simplified **real-time physics simulation** with **rigid body dynamics** and **frame-rate constraints** in **C++**, using basic physics integration and a fixed time step to maintain consistency.

This example uses the standard library for timing and console output and simulates a rigid body under gravity with basic collision detection (bouncing off walls). For real-world applications, consider using a physics engine like **Bullet**, **Box2D**, or **PhysX**.

---

```cpp
#include <iostream>
#include <chrono>
#include <thread>

class RigidBody {
public:
    RigidBody(float mass, float x, float y)
        : mass(mass), x(x), y(y), vx(0.0f), vy(0.0f), ax(0.0f), ay(0.0f) {}

    void applyForce(float fx, float fy) {
        ax = fx / mass;
        ay = fy / mass;
    }

    void update(float dt) {
        // Update velocity and position using Euler integration
        vx += ax * dt;
        vy += ay * dt;
        x += vx * dt;
        y += vy * dt;

        // Simple collision with walls (bounce)
        if (x < 0 || x > 100) vx *= -0.9f; // Damping
        if (y < 0 || y > 100) vy *= -0.9f;
    }

    void reset() {
        x = 50.0f;
        y = 50.0f;
        vx = 0.0f;
        vy = 0.0f;
    }

    float x, y, vx, vy, ax, ay;
    float mass;
};

int main() {
    RigidBody body(1.0f, 50.0f, 50.0f);
    const float gravity = -9.81f;
    const float fixedDeltaTime = 1.0f / 60.0f; // 60 FPS
    const float maxDeltaTime = 0.1f;

    auto lastTime = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();

    while (true) {
        auto now = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
        auto delta = std::chrono::duration<float>(now - lastTime).count();
        lastTime = now;

        // Cap delta time to avoid large steps
        if (delta > maxDeltaTime) delta = maxDeltaTime;

        // Apply gravity
        body.applyForce(0.0f, gravity);
        body.update(fixedDeltaTime);

        // Simulate rendering (console output)
        std::cout << "Position: (" << body.x << ", " << body.y << ")\n";

        // Sleep to maintain ~60 FPS
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(16));
    }

    return 0;
}
```

---

### 🔍 Explanation

- **RigidBody Class**: Represents a basic rigid body with position, velocity, and mass.
- **applyForce**: Updates acceleration based on applied forces.
- **update**: Integrates position and velocity, and applies simple wall collision.
- **Fixed Time Step**: Ensures physics updates occur at a consistent rate (60 FPS) regardless of rendering or input.
- **Frame-Rate Constraint**: Sleeps for a fixed interval to maintain 60 FPS.

---

### ⚠️ Notes

- This is a **simplified example** and lacks advanced features like multiple bodies, joints, or realistic collision resolution.
- For real-time applications, use a **physics engine** (e.g., **Bullet**, **Box2D**, or **PhysX**) and a **graphics library** (e.g., **OpenGL**, **SDL**, or **Vulkan**) for rendering.

```cpp
#include <iostream>
#include <chrono>
#include <thread>

// Simple Rigid Body Class
class RigidBody {
public:
    double x, y;       // Position
    double vx, vy;     // Velocity
    double ax, ay;     // Acceleration
    double mass;       // Mass

    RigidBody(double x, double y, double mass)
        : x(x), y(y), vx(0.0), vy(0.0), ax(0.0), ay(0.0), mass(mass) {}

    void applyForce(double fx, double fy) {
        ax += fx / mass;
        ay += fy / mass;
    }

    void update(double dt) {
        // Euler integration
        vx += ax * dt;
        vy += ay * dt;
        x += vx * dt;
        y += vy * dt;

        // Simple collision with boundaries
        if (x < 0 || x > 100) vx *= -1;
        if (y < 0 || y > 100) vy *= -1;

        // Reset acceleration
        ax = 0.0;
        ay = 0.0;
    }

    void printState() {
        std::cout << "Position: (" << x << ", " << y << ") | Velocity: (" << vx << ", " << vy << ")\n";
    }
};

int main() {
    const double fixedDeltaTime = 1.0 / 60.0; // 60 FPS target
    const double gravity = 9.81;              // m/s²
    RigidBody body(50.0, 50.0, 1.0);          // Initial position and mass

    auto startTime = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();

    while (true) {
        auto currentTime = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
        auto elapsed = std::chrono::duration<double>(currentTime - startTime).count();

        // Update physics at fixed time step
        if (elapsed >= fixedDeltaTime) {
            body.applyForce(0.0, -body.mass * gravity); // Apply gravity
            body.update(fixedDeltaTime);
            body.printState();

            startTime = currentTime; // Reset timer
        }

        // Sleep to maintain frame rate (approximate)
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(16)); // ~60 FPS
    }

    return 0;
}
```

- This is a **very simplified** simulation. Real physics engines (like [Bullet](https://bulletphysics.org/) or [PhysX](https://developer.nvidia.com/physx-sdk)) handle complex interactions, constraints, and optimizations.

#include <iostream>

```cpp
struct Body {
    float x, y;          // Position
    float vx, vy;        // Velocity
    float ax, ay;        // Acceleration
    float mass;          // Mass
    float width, height; // AABB dimensions

    Body(float x, float y, float mass, float width, float height)
        : x(x), y(y), vx(0), vy(0), ax(0), ay(0), mass(mass), width(width), height(height) {}

    void applyForce(float fx, float fy) {
        ax += fx / mass;
        ay += fy / mass;
    }

    void update(float dt) {
        vx += ax * dt;
        vy += ay * dt;
        x += vx * dt;
        y += vy * dt;
        ax = 0;
        ay = 0;
    }

    float getLeft() const { return x - width / 2; }
    float getRight() const { return x + width / 2; }
    float getTop() const { return y + height / 2; }
    float getBottom() const { return y - height / 2; }
};

class PhysicsWorld {
public:
    std::vector<Body> bodies;
    float timeStep = 1.0f / 60.0f; // Fixed time step (60 FPS)

    void addBody(Body body) {
        bodies.push_back(body);
    }

    void update(float dt) {
        // Apply gravity
        for (auto& body : bodies) {
            body.applyForce(0, body.mass * 9.81f); // Gravity
        }

        // Update positions
        for (auto& body : bodies) {
            body.update(dt);
        }

        // Collision detection
        for (size_t i = 0; i < bodies.size(); ++i) {
            for (size_t j = i + 1; j < bodies.size(); ++j) {
                const Body& b1 = bodies[i];
                const Body& b2 = bodies[j];

                // AABB collision check
                if (b1.getRight() >= b2.getLeft() &&
                    b1.getLeft() <= b2.getRight() &&
                    b1.getTop() >= b2.getBottom() &&
                    b1.getBottom() <= b2.getTop()) {
                    // Simple collision response: reverse velocities
                    std::swap(bodies[i].vx, bodies[j].vx);
                    std::swap(bodies[i].vy, bodies[j].vy);
                }
            }
        }
    }
};

int main() {
    PhysicsWorld world;

    // Add two bodies: one falling and one stationary
    world.addBody(Body(0, 0, 1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f));
    world.addBody(Body(2, 0, 1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f));

    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
    float accumulator = 0.0f;
    const float fixedTimeStep = 1.0f / 60.0f;

    while (true) {
        auto now = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
        float dt = std::chrono::duration<float>(now - start).count();
        start = now;

        accumulator += dt;

        while (accumulator >= fixedTimeStep) {
            world.update(fixedTimeStep);
            accumulator -= fixedTimeStep;

        // Output current positions (console-based simulation)

        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(16)); // ~60 FPS

    return 0;
}
```

```cpp
// Physics World
class PhysicsWorld {
public:
    std::vector<RigidBody> bodies;
    float gravity = 9.81f;

    void addBody(const RigidBody& body) {
        bodies.push_back(body);
    }

    // Update physics with fixed time step
    void update(float dt) {
        // Apply gravity
        for (auto& body : bodies) {
            body.vy += gravity * dt;
            body.x += body.vx * dt;
            body.y += body.vy * dt;
        }

        // Resolve collisions
        for (size_t i = 0; i < bodies.size(); ++i) {
            for (size_t j = i + 1; j < bodies.size(); ++j) {
                resolveCollision(bodies[i], bodies[j]);

    // Simple circle-circle collision resolution
    void resolveCollision(RigidBody& a, RigidBody& b) {
        float dx = b.x - a.x;
        float dy = b.y - a.y;
        float distance = std::sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy);
        float minDistance = a.radius + b.radius;

        if (distance < minDistance) {
            float overlap = minDistance - distance;
            float overlapX = dx / distance * overlap * 0.5f;
            float overlapY = dy / distance * overlap * 0.5f;

            a.y -= overlapY;
            b.x += overlapX;

            float vb = b.vx * nx + b.vy * ny;

            float impulse = (va - vb) / (1.0f / a.mass + 1.0f / b.mass);
            a.vx -= impulse * nx / a.mass;
            a.vy -= impulse * ny / a.mass;
            b.vx += impulse * nx / b.mass;
            b.vy += impulse * ny / b.mass;
        }
```

```cpp
#include <iostream>
#include <chrono>
#include <thread>
#include <btBulletDynamicsCommon.h>

int main() {
    // Initialize physics world
    btDefaultCollisionConfiguration collisionConfig;
    btCollisionDispatcher dispatcher(&collisionConfig);
    btBroadphaseInterface* broadphase = new btDbvtBroadphase();
    btSequentialImpulseConstraintSolver solver;
    btDiscreteDynamicsWorld dynamicsWorld(dispatcher, broadphase, &solver, &collisionConfig);
    dynamicsWorld.setGravity(btVector3(0, 0, -10));

    // Create a ground plane
    btStaticPlaneShape groundShape(btVector3(0, 1, 0), 0);
    btDefaultMotionState* groundMotionState = new btDefaultMotionState(btTransform(btQuaternion(0, 0, 0, 1), btVector3(0, -5, 0)));
    btRigidBody::btRigidBodyConstructionInfo groundRigidBodyInfo(0, groundMotionState, &groundShape);
    btRigidBody* groundRigidBody = btRigidBody::createRigidBody(groundRigidBodyInfo);
    dynamicsWorld.addRigidBody(groundRigidBody);

    // Create a falling box
    btBoxShape boxShape(btVector3(1, 1, 1));
    btDefaultMotionState* boxMotionState = new btDefaultMotionState(btTransform(btQuaternion(0, 0, 0, 1), btVector3(0, 10, 0)));
    btScalar mass = 1.0f;
    btVector3 inertia(0, 0, 0);
    boxShape.calculateLocalInertia(mass, inertia);
    btRigidBody::btRigidBodyConstructionInfo boxRigidBodyInfo(mass, boxMotionState, &boxShape, inertia);
    btRigidBody* boxRigidBody = btRigidBody::createRigidBody(boxRigidBodyInfo);
    dynamicsWorld.addRigidBody(boxRigidBody);

    // Simulation loop with frame-rate constraints (60 Hz)
    const btScalar fixedTimeStep = 1.0f / 60.0f;
    auto lastTime = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();

    while (true) {
        auto currentTime = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
        btScalar deltaTime = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::duration<btScalar>>(currentTime - lastTime).count();

        if (deltaTime >= fixedTimeStep) {
            dynamicsWorld.stepSimulation(fixedTimeStep, 10, fixedTimeStep);
            lastTime = currentTime;
        }

        // Optional: Render or log simulation state
        std::cout << "Box position: " << boxRigidBody->getWorldCenter() << std::endl;

        // Sleep to avoid CPU overuse
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(16)); // ~60 FPS
    }

    return 0;
}
```

```bash
pip install pybullet
```

```python
import pybullet as p
import pybullet_data
import time

# Initialize physics client

p.setAdditionalSearchPath(pybullet_data.getDataPath())
p.setGravity(0, 0, -9.81)  # Earth gravity

# Load ground plane
plane_id = p.loadURDF("plane.urdf")

# Load a rigid body (cube)
cube_id = p.loadURDF("cube.urdf", [0, 0, 1])  # Start 1m above ground

# Simulation parameters

frame_rate = 60
simulation_time = 10  # Total simulation time in seconds

# Simulation loop
start_time = time.time()
while time.time() - start_time < simulation_time:
    # Step simulation
    p.stepSimulation()

    # Frame-rate constraint: Sleep to maintain 60 FPS
    time.sleep(dt)

    # Optional: Print position of the cube

    print(f"Cube position: {pos}")

# Disconnect from physics client
```

```java
    SUCCESS, FAILURE, PENDING

// Payment processing service
class PaymentService {
    private final AccountRepository accountRepository;

    public PaymentService(AccountRepository accountRepository) {
        this.accountRepository = accountRepository;
    }

    public PaymentStatus processPayment(String fromAccountId, String toAccountId, BigDecimal amount) {
        if (amount == null || amount.compareTo(BigDecimal.ZERO) <= 0) {
            return PaymentStatus.FAILURE;
        }

        Account fromAccount = accountRepository.getAccount(fromAccountId);
        Account toAccount = accountRepository.getAccount(toAccountId);

        if (fromAccount == null || toAccount == null) {
            return PaymentStatus.FAILURE;
        }

        if (fromAccount.getBalance().compareTo(amount) < 0) {
            return PaymentStatus.FAILURE;
        }

        try {
            // Deduct amount from the source account
            BigDecimal newBalance = fromAccount.getBalance().subtract(amount);
            fromAccount.setBalance(newBalance);

            // Add amount to the destination account
            BigDecimal newToBalance = toAccount.getBalance().add(amount);
            toAccount.setBalance(newToBalance);

            // Save updated accounts
            accountRepository.updateAccount(fromAccount);
            accountRepository.updateAccount(toAccount);

            return PaymentStatus.SUCCESS;
        } catch (Exception e) {
            // Log the error (in a real system, logging would be handled by a framework)
            System.err.println("Payment processing failed: " + e.getMessage());
            return PaymentStatus.FAILURE;
        }
    }
}
```

```java
        this.cardNumber = cardNumber;
        this.amount = amount;

// Interface for payment validation
interface PaymentValidator {

}

// Interface for payment processing

    boolean processPayment(PaymentRequest request);
```
